guides.name-change-checklist.title: Name Change After Marriage: A US Checklist
guides.name-change-checklist.desc: The order of agencies, documents and accounts to update after a US marriage name change, plus what differs for other countries and for hyphenated names.
guides.name-change-checklist.lead: The sequence matters. Social Security comes before the DMV, the passport comes before international travel, and the marriage certificate is the document everything else depends on.
guides.name-change-checklist.f1v: Certified copies of the marriage certificate, typically 3–5
guides.name-change-checklist.f2v: Social Security, then DMV or state ID, then passport
guides.name-change-checklist.f3v: Employer, payroll, bank, cards, insurance, loans, voter registration
guides.name-change-checklist.f4v: Utilities, subscriptions, medical records, wills and beneficiaries
guides.name-change-checklist.s1: Start with several certified copies, not photocopies — agencies return them but often require an original. File with Social Security first and wait for the updated record to propagate before applying at the DMV, since state systems verify against it. Then update your passport, and only after that the long tail of private accounts.
guides.name-change-checklist.s2: This order is US-specific. In the UK a deed poll or marriage certificate is usually accepted directly by banks and the passport office, with no central registry step. In many European countries a change of surname after marriage is restricted or must be declared at the time of the marriage itself, and in some jurisdictions neither partner changes name. Some countries also require a spouse's consent or a court application.
guides.name-change-checklist.s3: Do not book international travel under a new name before the passport is updated — the ticket must match the passport exactly. Do not forget secondary records: professional licences, vehicle titles, TSA or trusted-traveller profiles, and beneficiary designations, which override a will. If you hyphenate or combine names, check that every system accepts the character length and punctuation.
guides.name-change-checklist.q1: How long does a name change take?
guides.name-change-checklist.a1: In the US, allow several weeks for Social Security and the DMV, and six to eleven weeks for a routine passport. Start as soon as you have the certificate.
guides.name-change-checklist.q2: Do I have to change my name?
guides.name-change-checklist.a2: No. In the US it is optional for either spouse, and many couples keep their names, hyphenate, or choose a new shared name where state law allows.
guides.name-change-checklist.q3: How many certified copies do I need?
guides.name-change-checklist.a3: Three to five is a practical starting point. Order more if several agencies will hold one at the same time.
